audience: Group CEO, COO, Chief Data & AI officer, CRO — pre-read before a first meeting
source_doc: Great Eastern Holdings Annual Report FY2025
notes: Every face sentence carries kind + support. kind=synthesis must be entailed by the cited released claims; kind=quote is verbatim; kind=question/offer/method are not findings. Resolver refuses any support id that is not released.

title.text: AI at Great Eastern: momentum, transition and the questions ahead

subtitle.text: An outside-in view from public disclosures  ·  Discussion document

footnote.text: Prepared by PLUMB Advisory from Great Eastern’s FY2025 Annual Report only. Not reviewed by Great Eastern. No management input.

title.text: Great Eastern has put AI to work in advice and claims; sustaining it now depends on leadership and governance clarity

head.text: AI is already in production where it touches customers most

body.text: Great Eastern has deployed an AI advisory platform for its financial advisers and rolled out a proprietary platform that automates medical claims; in 2025, 75% of medical claims were turned around the same day.

head.text: The leadership seat behind it was in transition

body.text: The report states that the Managing Director, Group Data and AI, was expected to join OCBC in March 2026, with a successor to be named in due course.

head.text: Governance of AI is asserted, but its framework is not described

body.text: The report commits to “discipline and robust governance” as AI use expands, but does not set out an AI risk framework, inventory or accountable owner.

callout.text: Five questions would turn this view into a basis for decisions — page 7

title.text: AI now spans the policy lifecycle, from advice to claims, with complex underwriting still in testing

items.text: AI advisory platform for financial advisers
In-house analytics and AI for underwriting
AI customer segmentation for instant approvals (Great CareShield)
Medical-bill OCR to detect wastage and abuse (Malaysia)
AI monitoring of transactions and sales for compliance risk
AI model to identify potential misconduct

legend_note.text: Status uses Great Eastern’s own verb for each initiative: deployed, rolled out, leveraged, sharpened or monitoring = in use; developed = developed; testing = testing.

title.text: Reported outcomes are material, but one is a result and the other a target

label.text: of medical claims turned around the same day

detail.text: “One of the fastest among Singapore’s health insurers”, based on Ministry of Health service indicators

label.text: targeted reduction in financial advisers’ preparation time

detail.text: The platform “aims to reduce” preparation time; no achieved figure is reported

so_what.text: Neither figure is reported with a baseline, a measurement period or a financial value — the evidence a board would need to scale either.

title.text: The executive who led Data and AI was expected to move to OCBC in March 2026

text.text: Data & AI operating model restructured “to accelerate transformation”
Managing Directors for Marketing, Customer and Digital, Premier Wealth and Regional Agency leave the Group
Marketing, Customer & Digital and Premier Wealth unified in a new Integrated Propositions and Platforms division
Managing Director, Group Data and AI, expected to join OCBC as Head of the Group Data Office

head.text: As at the FY2025 Annual Report

body.text: “The successors … will be named in due course.”

note.text: We have not verified whether a successor has since been appointed. This is Question 1.

title.text: The report asserts governance of AI but does not describe the framework behind it

items.text: AI use expanded “with discipline and robust governance”
Board competencies include artificial intelligence and risk management
Directors are to be paid for their contributions to IT infrastructure, data and AI initiatives
AI is used to monitor compliance risk — AI for governance, not governance of AI

right.head: What it does not set out

items.text: An AI policy or responsible-AI principles
An inventory of AI systems or their risk materiality
Model risk management applied to AI
A named executive accountable for AI risk

footnote.text: Full-text search of all 244 pages for 17 AI-governance terms (e.g. “responsible AI”, “model risk”, “FEAT”) returned no matches. OCBC group frameworks were not reviewed; absence from one document is not evidence of absence.

title.text: Five questions would turn this outside-in view into a basis for decisions

questions.text: Who now owns the Data and AI agenda, and did its scope change with the move to OCBC?
Where is the AI risk framework documented, and which parts are set by Great Eastern rather than OCBC group?
How complete is the inventory of AI systems, and how is each one rated for risk materiality?
How are the two 75% figures measured — baseline, period, population — and what are they worth?
What evidence would move complex-case underwriting AI from testing into production, and who decides?

title.text: A 12-day assessment would answer these questions with evidence, not opinion

columns.head: Where you stand
columns.body: AI maturity scored on eight dimensions, ranked against named Singapore insurers, with the evidence behind every score

columns.head: Why you win
columns.body: The three to five capabilities that pass a six-test right-to-win screen, and whether AI strengthens or erodes each

columns.head: Where AI pays
columns.body: Three to five value pools and the specific use cases that capture them, each tiered for AI risk

ask.text: What we need: time from 10–12 leaders. No confidential data is required for this phase.
